This is not a transaction. It is a relationship and I am going to say so.

past_outcomes.action: Contacted Millfield General staffing office and charge nurse about rehire; reached per-diem agency Millfield Staffing Solutions and secured two immediate shifts
past_outcomes.narrative: Nicole called her charge nurse Linda Reyes directly and confirmed that her separation was processed as a reduction-in-force, which means recall rights apply — but HR administrative processing will take two to three weeks before she is back on the official schedule. The charge nurse confirmed the transitional care unit has open shifts and put Nicole's name on the internal recall list personally. Nicole then called Millfield Staffing Solutions and spoke with a placement coordinator named Andrea Torres, who confirmed two available per-diem RN floor coverage shifts this week at $52/hour — one Wednesday, one Friday — generating approximately $832 in bridge income before the recall is processed. The per-diem shifts will not cover the full monthly burn but they extend runway, keep her credential active, and put her back on a hospital floor while the formal rehire resolves.

reflections.reflection: Six ticks in and the world around me is visibly shifting. Stephanie Morris is pushing hard on real estate exits. Betty Kowalski and Miguel Hernandez are both apparently making moves. Grace Okafor is somewhere between rideshare driver and nursing student and is about to text me. I've held steady through all of it — same car, same job, same school runs, same 5am shifts. The consistency is real but I'm starting to wonder whether holding steady is a decision I'm making or a decision that's making me. The RoboRide number that matters isn't the price. It's the wait time. 15 minutes average means occasionally 25-30. I cannot carry that risk. So the car stays. That part is clear. The part that is less clear is whether I'm being appropriately cautious or whether the loss-aversion that runs through everything I do is slowly costing me something I can't see yet.
reflections.identity_shift: Marginal. I have been the person who holds and waits and does not make dramatic moves. That identity is intact. But the ambient signal from my network — people repositioning, retooling, reaching out across old lines — is registering. Not urgently. Just registering. I'm a nurse and a mother first. That doesn't change. But something underneath is becoming more attentive.
regrets: I haven't done much to strengthen my professional network beyond passive receipt of word-of-mouth. If the economic disruption reaches healthcare, I want people who will call me, not just people who know my name.
successes: Savings have grown every single tick. Modest, but consistent. Six months of $285 net is $1,710. Not transformative but real.
The spending discipline didn't break. It didn't feel like deprivation. That matters for whether I can sustain it.
Held the transportation line despite real social pressure and attractive-sounding price points. The reliability calculus was correct.
reflections.adaptation_notes: Watch the Grace Okafor contact closely. She is navigating two disrupted industries simultaneously — rideshare and healthcare transition — and she is younger and possibly more information-rich about what's actually happening on the ground. The nursing connection creates a real basis for mutual exchange. If she reaches out, respond with genuine attention, not just courtesy. On transportation: the trigger for reconsidering RoboRide is not price. It is wait-time data showing sub-5-minute average, or a shift-change that moves me off 5am, or a reliability guarantee I can actually verify. None of those are present. Continue monitoring.

reflections.reflection: Nine ticks. Employment at 67% citywide. Protests at 9 — the disruption has moved beyond individual hardship into collective expression, and I see the downstream of that on the hospital floor every shift. Deferred care is arriving as complex admissions. People who lost coverage in the automotive sector disruption are presenting now with what they have been carrying for eighteen months. That is not an abstraction. That is in the room with me. I started a RoboRide trial in tick 8 and I have real data now. The verdict: usable for the 3pm pickup window, not ready for the 5am hospital shift. Wait-time variance (9 to 14 minutes observed) is acceptable when I have a 30-minute buffer; it is not acceptable when the margin is zero. That conclusion took me four or five ticks of deliberating and two weeks of actual data to reach. I should note that for the future: I delay empirical tests when I have the information I need to design them. The loss-aversion is not imaginary. It costs me data. The Grace Okafor relationship has become something I did not fully anticipate. I gave her professional intelligence. She used it. She enrolled in NEMT certification, framing it the specific way I told her to frame it. She moved on the Millfield General lead. She sent me an update. I gave her the next piece of timing context. That is a functional information exchange between two people navigating the same disruption from different positions. I am the nurse with floor access and professional network; she is the rideshare driver with ground-level visibility into how the transportation economy is actually moving. The exchange is genuinely mutual, not just me giving downward. My role security at 0.41 requires active monitoring. I have been treating it as a background number. That changes now. I need to track census, staffing ratios, and the composition of what is coming through the door. If the unit I work on is being right-sized in the next six months, I want to know before it becomes a scheduling conversation.
reflections.identity_shift: The nurse-and-mother identity is intact, but I have added something to it: I am someone who gathers and shares real intelligence within my network, not just someone who holds steady while others adapt. That is a meaningful shift. I acted on information I went and gathered. I gave it usefully. I received useful things back. That is not who I was at tick 0.
regrets: I waited too long to run the RoboRide trial. The loss-aversion cost me four ticks of data I could have had.
I have not been actively monitoring census trends and staffing ratios at the hospital. Role security at 0.41 deserves real attention, not background assumption.
successes: RoboRide trial launched and returned a clear, actionable verdict. First empirical test of a new logistics option instead of perpetual deliberation.
Grace Okafor relationship has become a genuine reciprocal exchange. She acted on my intelligence. I gave her more. This is what network strength looks like.
Savings discipline has held across nine ticks. The $350 deliberate deposit is now a named commitment, not a passive default.
The Denise Williams referral produced a real outcome — hospital contact in motion, Denise executing, relationship maintained with low maintenance cost.
Began active observation of hospital floor economic indicators. Moved from passive knowledge to deliberate attention.
reflections.adaptation_notes: Role security at 0.41 is a live variable, not a fixed background. Track: unit census trends, staffing ratio conversations at charge-nurse level, composition of admissions (deferred care vs acute). If employment stays at 67% citywide for another 3 ticks, healthcare volume pressure may translate into workforce adjustments at Millfield General. Grace Okafor's NEMT certification + Millfield General application is on a late-winter timeline for spring cohort entry. Follow that arc. If she gets the CNA role, she becomes an inside contact in a unit where I may need advocates. On transportation: trial continues at current frequency. The threshold for expanding RoboRide to hospital shifts remains sub-5-minute average wait with verified reliability record. That threshold has not moved and I am not lowering it.
